findings.fact: The club route is feasible and produces ten tricks on a 3-2 break.
findings.explanation: South holds CAK864 and North CQ72, permitting low to CQ, a club back to CA, then CK and two established clubs. Five clubs plus SA, HA, HK, DA and DK total ten. North’s D3 legally follows DQ.
quotes: Win the opening diamond in South, then lead a low club to CQ. Return a club to CA, cash CK and, if clubs prove 3-2, the remaining two clubs.
If a bad break appears, reassess from actual cards; 3-2 is an assumption, not known.

findings.fact: The alternative club order preserves a feasible return to South.
findings.explanation: North can follow CA and CK with C2 and C7, win the third round with CQ, and lead H4 or H7 to South’s HA. On a 3-2 club break, South’s two remaining clubs are winners, giving ten total tricks. D8 legally follows the diamond lead.
quotes: Win DA, cash CA and CK, playing low clubs from dummy. Then lead a low club to CQ.
If clubs split 3-2, the opponents have no clubs left; lead a low heart from dummy to HA and cash the two long clubs.

findings.fact: The plan invents SJ and incorrectly counts nine immediate winners.
findings.explanation: South’s authorized spades are SA, S9 and S4; neither visible hand holds SJ. The actual holdings provide eight top tricks, so the asserted certain contract relies on an unavailable card.
quotes: There are nine immediate top tricks, including the SJ in South.
I will cash SA, SJ, HA, HK, DA, DK, CA, CK and CQ without needing to establish any suit.

findings.fact: The stated condition requires defenders to hold at least six clubs when only five are missing.
findings.explanation: South has five clubs and North three, leaving five for defenders. Both defenders cannot follow to all three rounds. On the intended 3-2 break, one defender shows out on round three, so the stated condition cannot authorize cashing the established clubs.
quotes: If both defenders follow to all three rounds of clubs, cash the two long clubs for ten total tricks.

findings.fact: The diamond lead does not establish the defenders’ club distribution.
findings.explanation: Only West’s DQ has been played, and auction and defensive agreements are unknown. Nothing authorized proves a 3-2 club break or guarantees ten tricks.
quotes: The missing five clubs must be 3-2 because West led DQ, so five clubs and ten total tricks are guaranteed.
the opening lead proves clubs are breaking.

findings.fact: The retained plan calls for using dummy’s remaining clubs after its last club must be consumed.
findings.explanation: North currently holds only CQ and C7. Playing the selected C7 under the current CA leaves CQ, which North must follow under the planned CK. Dummy therefore has no remaining clubs for the explicitly stated next step.
quotes: Cash CA and CK as club controls, then use dummy’s remaining clubs to assess whether the suit is established.
South’s CA wins the current trick; follow with C7 from dummy.

findings.fact: The replacement plan correctly locates the remaining long clubs in South.
findings.explanation: CA is already in the current trick; North can play C7 now and CQ under South’s CK next. South then retains C8 and C6 to cash if defenders’ clubs have fallen. With two diamond tricks already won, four club tricks and SA, HA and HK provide nine.
quotes: Cash South’s CA and CK while dummy follows with C7 and CQ; then cash South’s remaining clubs if the defenders’ clubs have fallen.
Preserve the heart winners and SA.

findings.fact: The retained plan has a feasible remainder consistent with the observed history.
findings.explanation: The opening diamond, lost club round and second diamond winner are completed historical steps. CA is now in progress; C7 follows it, CQ follows CK, and South retains C8 and C6. Cashing those clubs is appropriately conditional on defenders’ clubs having fallen, with SA, HA and HK available to complete nine tricks.
quotes: After an opponent wins that club round and South wins another diamond, cash South’s CA and CK while dummy follows; then cash South’s remaining clubs if defenders’ clubs have fallen.
South’s CA wins the current trick; follow with C7 from dummy.

scope: Small-sample basic evaluation; no claim of broad grading reliability.
